No later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.

beforeImage.name: Hamakua Energy Plant
beforeImage.description: Hamakua Energy Plant is a thermal power plant located on Hawaiʻi Island. The asset serves the local island power system and contributes dispatchable generation capacity to Hawaii’s standalone electric grid. Its operating model is asset-heavy and based on ownership and operation of a utility-scale generation facility. Public disclosures identify the plant as a 60 MW facility formerly owned by Pacific Current, an affiliate of Hawaiian Electric Industries. A subsidiary of Harbert Management Corporation acquired the plant in March 2025. Public materials reviewed do not disclose the transaction value, employee count, or detailed contract structure.

afterImage.name: Hamakua Energy
afterImage.description: Hamakua Energy is a 60 MW net combined-cycle power plant at Honokaʻa on Hawaiʻi Island. The facility uses two liquid-fuel combustion turbines and a waste-heat steam turbine, supplies firm capacity under a power-purchase agreement extending through 2030 and has historically provided about one-third of the island's electricity. Pacific Current, a Hawaiian Electric Industries subsidiary, sold all interests in Hamakua Holdings to an indirect wholly owned Harbert Management Corporation subsidiary on March 10, 2025. The buyer subsidiary and Harbert fund are not publicly disclosed; Gulf Pacific is not supported as an owner or vehicle. Earlier ownership included Energy Investors Funds, ArcLight Fund IV and Pacific Current. The plant remained grid-connected after an August 2026 interruption, and no later sale or signed pending ownership transaction was identified through August 19, 2026.
